1: Internal stock. No courier. Let's find who was at Delivery.
My theory has a secret tunnel and a minivan.
Not yet. I've drawn it a question mark to park beside.
Good. The minivan was blocking my notes.
2: The Cup has returned itself with suspiciously good posture.
Can its excellent posture tell us who brought it back?
You take the map, Detective. I'll watch the extremely well-behaved Cup.
3: I have found a sparkle. I am calling it Inspector Glitter.
Has Inspector Glitter actually found a difference?
Should I be worried about my job?
Only if you start shedding glitter. Pass me Photo B.
4: I'm watching the box for suspicious movements.
If it moves, we can all be impressed. Who carried it?
I can make it blink first.
If you manage that, I'm giving the box your helmet.
5: I challenge you to beat my locker.
Does it know this is a competition?
Then we shall read its clues politely.
If the locker wins, does it get a badge?
6: I had plans for that dragon tooth.
So did I. None of them involved stirring soup.
Perhaps the dragon was a cook.
That explains the spoon. Slight problem with the Romans.
We'll ask about the label before we rewrite history.
A relief. I've only just put history back on its shelves.
Can we keep the dragon in the margin?
Pencil only. I'd like a chance to object.
7: Alio, how many cupboards have you checked?
The dramatic ones. Then the large ones.
The moon costume is larger than most cupboards.
Exactly. Now we can stop opening tiny doors.
Good. I was starting to introduce myself to the brooms.
8: Have you shown it to the walls?
The building has rejected my first draft.
Then let's find out where it will let us through.
I'll hold the map. No folding the building to make it fit.
9: Something looks familiar. That isn't the same as knowing.
Then we'll find something you can check it against.
I remember being promised cake on an investigation.
You promised yourself the cake, Alio.
A very reliable source. Terrible at delivery.
10: Two teams. One rover. I refuse to split it down the middle.
Generous. The wheels would be awkward.
We'll check who actually had access.
While you do, can I untangle that cable?
Careful. It may have a third owner.
11: Your phone has been living beside the oat bar.
I would like that entered in the bag report.
12: Please speak clearly for the notebook.
I've got that. What about the password?
I think it has set a price.
I'll ask the handler. My first interview with a snack budget.
13: My fox theory has one weakness.
It needs somewhere to keep the camera.
A tiny camera strap. I'll draw one.
At last. Someone taking the equipment problem seriously.
Now you've got me wondering about the strap. Hand me the actual photo before this gets worse.
14: One of these statements has broken the clock.
Or somebody mixed up two moments.
Could happen. I once announced I'd packed lunch. I'd packed three books.
I remember. Your bag was very well fed.
Not a crumb. Three books and not one on cooking.
15: I was going to suggest satellite tracking.
Ruthless. You've beaten me with a piece of cardboard.
16: That hat could shelter the whole team.
It also had an excellent detective underneath it.
The hat is not admissible dating evidence.
Can we still admire it respectfully?
17: Then perhaps its first assignment can be reading the ticket sleeve.
Does the helmet earn travel points?
Only if it buys its own ticket.
18: Can your watch accept being wrong?
It is handling the news with dignity.
Less gracefully. I am correcting the record.
I'll check the new times. You can tell the watch it hasn't lost its job.
19: I was going to say 'digital ghost'.
I'm checking the scanner first. The ghost can wait outside.
In a library? It'll complain about the silence.
I'll find it something to read.
A paper one. I'm not giving it the Wi-Fi password.
20: This panel looks like a very worried pear.
Can I have the panel before you frame it?
It's looking very nervous. Be nice.
Does the pear have an alibi?
21: Stay here. I need you to check the joins with me.
Keep the handwriting visible. It may matter once the edges fit.
Do you know whose it is?
Maybe. The archive will have to back me up.
Detective, you fit the pieces. I'll check every join.
22: Three identical black instrument cases. Excellent. Objects have joined witness protection.
Their names are on the labels.
Not everyone is cut out for a life undercover.
They've had a long rehearsal. Can we get them home?
I'll check the shelves. I'm not reading a bedtime story to an instrument case.
23: The arcade scoreboard has challenged me personally.
I've got the wristband file. Can you bear to leave your rival unsupervised?
For the case. Tell it I haven't surrendered.
24: I have paused my dramatic theory.
Yes. I thought I'd see what the mud had to say first.
Both of you? I should photograph this.
Footprints first. My good behaviour can wait for the family album.
25: This parcel has met a lot of people. Has anyone asked where it wants to go?
Let's find out before somebody helpfully moves it again.
I'll guard it. No unauthorised helping.
For us. The parcel has had quite enough people trying to improve its day.
26: Empty rooms. We've been looking at everyone except nobody.
I'm telling your brothers you said that.
A historic moment. Detective, pull your maps closer before they recover.
27: Clean hands. Flat map. No heroic folding.
What about a small heroic point?
One finger. A landmark. I can allow it.
We solved a parcel just to earn permission for one finger.
28: I have put my tunnel proposal on a separate card.
How much evidence is on the card?
I'd like a card. Some of my very organised plans are mostly that.
Make it two. I used to call mine 'experience'.
29: That's a lot of map. I'll clear some space.
Take your time. We are not going anywhere.
I can be quiet for one map.
I've written that down. In pencil, to be fair.
Make the call when you're ready.
30: Case Wall ready? Then the panel's yours.
And the victory noise is mine.
Keep it in your head until the door opens.
Mine's already getting a bit loud in there.
Go on, Detective. We'll be right behind you.
